why_ai: Licensed nurses, physicians and surgeons treat acutely ill patients in person, carry personal liability, and make high-stakes calls on deterioration and surgery that demand will not hand to software.
why_clarity: Protocols, DRGs and CMS measures codify much of the work, but every admission differs and outcomes such as readmission and mortality surface weeks later through noisy, risk-adjusted measures.
why_digital: Care is delivered on patients' bodies in a local building; patients arrive by ambulance, referral and network, not online.

why_ai: Claims, denials and contract variances are screen work that AI-native revenue-cycle vendors target directly; only the clinical argument and the payer negotiation keep some judgement in house.
why_clarity: Each claim is paid, denied or underpaid against written rules and contracts at enormous volume, though appeal outcomes arrive months later.
why_digital: Remittances, charts and contracts are worked entirely on screen, often by outsourced or offshore teams.

why_ai: Physician advisors and denial nurses argue contested medical necessity, and peer-to-peer calls need a licensed clinician, but evidence assembly and drafting are being automated.
why_clarity: Criteria and appeal levels are written down, but each case turns on its chart and the payer's reading, and overturns arrive weeks or months later.
why_digital: Denials, charts and appeals are digital documents worked on screen; peer-to-peer happens by phone.

why_ai: Recomputing expected payment from contract terms is rule-bound reconciliation that extraction and pricing engines absorb.
why_clarity: Each remittance line either matches the contract or not, across millions of near-identical lines, checkable once terms are structured.
why_digital: Contracts and 835 files are digital, and recovery firms work them remotely on contingency.

why_ai: Scheduling is screen work, but block allocation is negotiated with surgeons, and the value is delivered as staffed, physical OR time.
why_clarity: Utilisation, overtime and cancellations are measured daily, though block policy is political and case durations vary by patient.
why_digital: Case logs and schedules are digital; the outcome is a physical room in use, and vendors sell to perioperative committees.

why_ai: Filling shifts is coordination that matching software can do, but the safety judgement on each unit's mix and the nurses themselves stay human and local.
why_clarity: A shift is filled or not, every day, with ratios and costs known immediately, though rules and fairness vary by contract.
why_digital: Schedules are digital, but the supply is local nurses showing up in person, bought through local staffing offices and agencies.

why_ai: Licensed RN case managers and social workers judge level of care and guide families through hard choices under discharge-planning rules, while packet assembly and chasing are automatable.
why_clarity: Avoidable days and placement times are counted, but each patient's needs, family and payer differ.
why_digital: Referrals move by portal, phone and fax to local facilities; families are met in person at the bedside.

why_ai: Revenue-cycle, cost-report and quality submissions for small hospitals automate, but a CFO signs the cost report and the hospital buys from a named consultant or network it trusts.
why_clarity: Cost-based reimbursement rules, claim edits and CMS measure specifications define the work, though each small hospital's mix of services and staff gaps differs and audit outcomes lag.
why_digital: Ledgers, claims and EHR data are digital and much of the work is outsourced remotely, with networks and consultants still visiting on site.

why_ai: Bedside nurses assess, treat and watch patients in person under their own licence, and their vigilance is the hospital's first defence against deterioration.
why_clarity: Assessments follow written protocols and recur every shift, but whether a judgement was right shows only hours or days later.
why_digital: Nursing is delivered on patients' bodies on a hospital unit; documentation is the only digital part.

why_ai: Coding and CDI review read records against codified rules, a task NLP increasingly performs, though credentialed coders and audit accountability keep humans signing complex DRGs.
why_clarity: ICD-10 guidelines and the MS-DRG grouper codify the task and it recurs per discharge, but payer audit outcomes arrive months later.
why_digital: Charts, codes and queries are digital, and coding is widely outsourced and done remotely.

why_ai: Eligibility, authorisation and estimates are rule lookups and portal submissions that payer APIs and agents are absorbing.
why_clarity: Each service is authorised, verified and priced or not, at high volume, with denials showing errors quickly.
why_digital: Orders, payer rules and portals are digital, and pre-service work is commonly centralised or outsourced.

why_ai: Epidemiologists and health economists design studies whose credibility depends on accountable method, and buyers keep paying for a unique de-identified corpus, though benchmark production itself is computational.
why_clarity: Benchmarks and study protocols are codified and repeat across clients, though study validity is judged slowly by reviewers.
why_digital: De-identified data in, studies and licences out, sold remotely to life-science and hospital buyers.

why_ai: Specialists who sign cost reports and argue DSH and S-10 positions before MACs and the PRRB carry accountability, but routine preparation is automatable.
why_clarity: Cost-report rules and recovery formulas are written down and repeat by hospital, with audit outcomes arriving a year or more later.
why_digital: Cost and claims data are worked on screen, and firms serve hospitals nationwide remotely.

why_ai: Software reads charts for missed severity, with clinician reviewers confirming; AI-native vendors substitute much of the manual review.
why_clarity: Findings are checkable against coding rules and recur per discharge, though payer audit outcomes lag.
why_digital: Charts and findings move digitally and vendors sell nationally.

why_ai: Licensed physicians make and defend contested status decisions in peer-to-peer calls, though prediction software takes the screening.
why_clarity: Criteria exist, but each status decision turns on a patient's chart, and payer outcomes arrive later.
why_digital: Reviews are done remotely on charts and by phone for hospitals across the country.

why_ai: Credentialed appraisers sign opinions that hospitals and counsel rely on in Stark and AKS matters, and the signature carries the value.
why_clarity: Methods and survey benchmarks are standard and the opinions repeat, but whether an opinion was right shows only if regulators challenge it.
why_digital: Contracts and survey data are digital, and opinions are delivered remotely as reports.

why_ai: Protocol-bound survey fielding and benchmark reporting are commodity work that software and AI analysis of comments absorb.
why_clarity: CMS fixes the instrument, sampling and submission dates, and results are scored the same way every quarter.
why_digital: Surveys go out by mail, phone and web, and results are delivered digitally to hospitals nationwide.

why_ai: Society-run registries are trusted because clinicians govern them, and CMS coverage rules and public reporting sustain demand.
why_clarity: Data definitions and risk models are standardised and the reports recur quarterly, though outcomes are judged slowly.
why_digital: Abstracted data arrive electronically and reports are delivered online to participating hospitals.

why_ai: Forecasts are computed from licensed claims and public data, a product AI-native analytics can replicate; buyers pay partly for the firm's brand with boards.
why_clarity: Methods differ by firm and ten-year forecasts are graded only years later, if ever.
why_digital: Data, models and subscriptions are entirely digital and sold remotely.

why_ai: Insurers bear the risk and coded claims need clinical and legal judgement, and hospitals will keep buying liability cover and its risk advice.
why_clarity: Claims are coded to a taxonomy, but each case is distinct and claims close years after the event.
why_digital: Claim files are digital, but coverage is sold through brokers and relationships.

why_ai: Internal strategy and analytics teams make consequential, ambiguous calls for system leadership that boards will not hand to outside software.
why_clarity: Analyses vary by question and their effects show up slowly in operating results.
why_digital: Work is on screen inside the system, serving an internal client rather than an open market.

why_ai: Forecasting and scheduling software is a commodity-prone category where EHR vendors and AI-native newcomers compete directly.
why_clarity: Utilisation and census predictions are scored daily against what happened.
why_digital: Operational data in, software out, sold remotely to health systems.

why_ai: Measure development needs statisticians and clinicians accountable to CMS rulemaking, and the programmes keep growing.
why_clarity: Specifications and re-evaluations are codified and recur annually, with validation against claims.
why_digital: Federal claims data in, specifications and reports out, procured through federal contracts.

why_ai: Ratings are computed from public data by small teams, and the brand of the rater is most of what is sold.
why_clarity: Methods are published but contested, and whether a grade predicts outcomes is rarely tested.
why_digital: Public data in, ratings and badge licences out, all online.

why_ai: Clinical prediction that drives treatment is regulated and validated on each population, but EHR vendors offer free alternatives.
why_clarity: Events are defined and frequent, but sepsis definitions disagree and the clinician's own action confounds the label.
why_digital: EHR data in, models out, sold to health systems remotely.

why_ai: Statutory regulators set budgets and targets with legal force, and the role grows as states take on hospital costs.
why_clarity: Rate-setting rules are written, but their effects on prices and care are contested and slow to observe.
why_digital: Filings and discharge data are digital; the work is done for one state's hospitals under statute.

why_ai: Compiling member discharge data into standard reports is routine analysis that software automates; the association relationship sustains it.
why_clarity: Reports follow fixed formats and recur each quarter or year.
why_digital: Member data in, reports out online, within one state's membership.
